I appreciate that you've had those conversations, but a consensus among the people in your circle doesn't really change the substance of my view. 

There is substantial empirical research linking heavy social media usage to negative mental health outcomes—especially in adolescents—alongside measurable increases in societal polarization and the degradation of public discourse. While the connective benefits are real, the core business models are built to monetize outrage and optimize for engagement at the expense of well-being.

I'm always open to examining new data and arguments, but simply knowing others disagree isn't a reason to abandon a well-reasoned perspective. What specific arguments did your colleagues make that you found convincing?
